data.title: bn-36wy3: per-task cancel phases, single-task deadline cancellation, subtree-scoped ledgers (RFC 0026 corr. 53)

data.body:
[high] Preserve race detection when cancellation events are projected out

The CancelRequest branch sets CancelTrack.by_region only inside observes_cancellation(). BindingConfig permits cancellation-family projection while lifecycle remains mandatory. In that configuration, an own-region cancellation after a task deadline expires but before its next poll loses the by_region marker. single_cancel then emits lifecycle CancelRequested and Cancel instead of returning CancelRaced. The same journal already contains RegionCancelRequested, so the repository lift rejects the returned evidence as CancelAlreadyRequested. This lets binding::run return evidence that its own calculus rejects.

The RFC requires refusal for this own-region deadline race. Track by_region for every substrate CancelRequest. Apply the family guard only to emitted CancellationEvent data and pending-request bookkeeping.

Failure modes: The binding returns a journal that contradicts the calculus. A caller can accept evidence that the independent lift rejects.

Edge cases: This needs own-region cancellation after deadline expiry and before the next poll, with Family::Cancellation omitted. Parent cancellation stays distinct because its stronger cause wins.

Rollback: Revert the deadline-binding slice, or record by_region outside the family guard while preserving event projection.

Monitoring: Count generated journals that fail the lift. Compare CancelRaced results across all family configurations.

Validation: Replay the same schedule for lifecycle-only and every family projection. Require CancelRaced with no journal. Also require every returned journal to lift as Conforms.

The separate risk:critical human-approval gate remains mandatory. This static review cannot waive it.

data.reason: High: cancellation-family projection suppresses own-region deadline-race detection and can return a journal that the calculus rejects. See th-2wpjer. The separate risk:critical human-approval gate remains mandatory.

data.body: Fixed in 5171702. binding.rs now records every substrate CancelRequest in region_requested, unconditionally, and single_cancel checks that set. The family guard now covers only the emitted CancellationEvent, pending_requests and the phases record. I audited all 24 observes_*() guards in binding.rs. The same pattern (a substrate fact that decides a refusal, inside a projection guard) was also in four other places, all now unconditional: cause_of on the CancelRequest reason; the cancelled completion's cause_of and the cancellation-oracle confirmation (region Complete arm and single_cancel); check_cancellation_protocol in run(); cross_check_ledger in finish(). The rest are emission-only or emission buffers: channel_event, Advanced, settled, Opened/SendersClosed, the spawn Deadline event, time Scheduled/Fired/Cancelled buffers, effect Reserved/Committed/Aborted with pending_aborts, obligation Opened/Discharged/Transferred with pending_discharges, and observe_ack phases. Two refusals depend on the observed families by design, because the family has no event for them: ReservationDropped and the unobserved ObligationLeak. New tests: the_race_is_refused_under_every_projection (CancelRaced with no journal under all 32 projections) and every_journal_the_binding_returns_under_any_projection_conforms (1092 deadline logs x 32 projections, all Conforms). All asupersync tests pass. just check: all pass except the lead-owned security-review-present.

Verified at 5171702 across every projection path. `region_requested`, cause mapping, the cancellation oracle, and ledger cross-check now remain outside family guards. The new 32-projection tests cover the original race.

Thus  makes each region-cancelled worker that did not explicitly acknowledge report . The same worker reports . data.body:
[medium] Complete finding; the first comment lost identifiers during command transport.

`cancel_phase` derives a region-only request only from the current region state. `cancel` changes that state to `Draining(Cancelled)`, but `finalize` replaces it with `Finalized`. No worker field records the region request. Thus `cancel -> drain -> finalize` makes each region-cancelled worker that did not explicitly acknowledge report `CancelPhase::Active`. The same worker reports `WorkerState::Cancelled`. This contradicts the API promise that a terminated worker keeps the phase it reached. It creates an impossible machine state with cancellation completed but never requested.

Persist the region-originated request on each affected worker, or preserve equivalent per-worker state after finalization. Add a regression that queries `cancel_phase` after finalization for workers cancelled only by their region.

Failure modes: Post-finalization evidence can say a cancelled worker was never requested. A downstream checker can derive a false lifecycle history.

Edge cases: Root and ancestor cancellation both reproduce it. Created, Running, and Suspended workers reproduce it. An explicitly acknowledged worker stays `Acknowledged` and hides the defect. Repeated region cancellation must remain idempotent.

Rollback: Revert the public per-task phase claim, or store the region request before finalization while preserving existing drain behavior.

Monitoring: Assert that no `WorkerState::Cancelled` worker reports `CancelPhase::Active`. Compare phase snapshots before and after every finalization.

Validation: Test cancel, drain, and finalize for root and child subtrees across all three live worker states. Require the phase after finalization to equal the phase before finalization. Re-run the calculus differential and binding lift corpus.

The separate risk:critical human-approval gate remains mandatory. This static review cannot waive it.

Fixed in 449cbd6. RegionTree::cancel now sets a per-worker region_requested flag on every live worker of the cancelled subtree. The flag is idempotent, so a repeated cancel changes nothing. cancel_phase now reads only the recorded flags (own request, region request, acknowledgement), not the region's current state, so the phase a worker reached survives finalize. settle debug-asserts Cancelled => phase != Active. New test a_region_cancellation_s_request_survives_finalization covers a root subtree, a child subtree and an ancestor's cancel, over created, running, parked, acknowledged and already-completed workers. Phases after finalize equal phases before, a repeated cancel changes neither phases nor the ledger, and no cancelled worker is Active. The interleaving sweep asserts the invariant after every teardown. The continuumd differential and every PR-14 lift corpus pass unchanged, so journal bytes are stable. just check: all pass except the lead-owned security-review-present.
Verified at 449cbd6847cd. WorkerRecord now preserves region_requested after finalization, and cancel_phase reads the stored flag.

data.body: [HIGH][risk:high] finish validates only Cancelled workers against reported phases. It never validates reported phases against worker state. CancellationEvent::Cancelled records Phase::Cancelled without completing the model worker at lines 477-499. Therefore, a deadline journal truncated after cancellation completion but before Lifecycle TaskStep::Cancel returns Conforms with a live worker. Requested or Acknowledged phases can also remain unfinished at journal end. This permits silent certification of contradictory or incomplete cancellation evidence. 1) Failure modes: lift accepts incomplete deadline or region cancellation, and downstream consumers trust false conformance. 2) Edge cases: prefixes ending in Requested, Acknowledged, or Cancelled; especially the pinned deadline sequence before its final lifecycle cancel. 3) Rollback: withdraw this lift path, or require every tracked phase to reconcile bidirectionally with the final worker state. 4) Monitoring: count conforming lifts with a tracked phase whose worker is not Cancelled. Alert on any nonzero count. 5) Input validation: truncate the pinned deadline journal after CancellationEvent::Cancelled and require a violation. Also reject journals ending in Requested or Acknowledged. Retain conforming complete deadline and region journals. This BLOCK does not satisfy or replace the separate risk:critical human-approval gate.

data.reason: [HIGH] cancellation::finish accepts a tracked Cancelled, Requested, or Acknowledged phase without a matching terminal worker state. A truncated deadline journal can therefore return Conforms before Lifecycle TaskStep::Cancel.

data.body: Fixed in fb8d74c. A journal that ends inside a protocol now lifts as Inconclusive(InsufficientTelemetry) through the new LiftStop::Incomplete(Family), never as Conforms. cancellation::finish now requires every reported phase to have ended: phase cancelled, and the worker Cancelled in the calculus. A requested or acknowledged phase, or a cancelled phase whose drain or cancel step is missing, is Incomplete. The new lifecycle::finish refuses a region still Draining(Cancelled), a drained region not finalized, and a task requested alone that has not ended. Audit of the other finishes: obligation already refuses an unsettled finalized region (Unsettled); time already refuses a due timer that has not fired (Late); effect and channel already refuse a terminal holder (LeakedAtClose, SendOutlivesTask, ReceiverOutlivesTask). A live holder of a reservation, an open obligation, an armed timer that is not due, or a blocked send or receive is a state a real run can end in, so those stay admitted. The A7 model gained the same end condition (docs/02 section 7: region cancelling and undrained, or drained and not finalized), so model and lift agree. Completeness notion: a prefix is mid-protocol if it ends inside one of six things: an unabsorbed cancellation phase, a single-task cancellation not ended, a region cancel not drained, a drain not finalized, a finalize not settled (when the prefix carries the obligations family), or a due timer not fired. Every other prefix is complete. Completeness is relative to the families a prefix carries, because a journal has no alphabet header. Sweeps: every strict prefix of all 7873 A7 corpus journals (100k mid-protocol prefixes refused, 215k complete ones conform, and the model agrees on each), plus every prefix of the 7572-log deadline corpus. Anti-vacuity: a deadline journal cut before its cancel is Inconclusive, and conforms once that event is restored. just check: all pass except the lead-owned security-review-present.

Verified at fb8d74c6a521. The new finish checks reject ordinary prefixes ending at requested, acknowledged, or phase-cancelled before model termination. This closes the original truncation finding. A separate cross-path absorption finding follows.

data.reason: Original prefix-truncation finding fixed at fb8d74c6a521; separate cross-path blocker recorded.

data.body:
[HIGH][risk:high] Require the single-task cancel step, not any Cancelled state

`requested_alone_unended` at crates/continuum-asupersync/src/family/cancellation.rs:530-534 treats any `WorkerState::Cancelled` as the end of an own-task cancellation. The lifecycle finish relies on that result at crates/continuum-asupersync/src/family/lifecycle.rs:419-420. A wire journal can therefore contain lifecycle `cancel-requested`, omit lifecycle `cancel`, then add a region cancel, drain, and finalize. The region drain sets the worker to `Cancelled`, so both finish checks pass and `lift` returns `Conforms`. With the cancellation family present, `requested(deadline) -> acknowledged -> cancelled(deadline)` can be absorbed by the same later region drain. This contradicts the independent completeness rule at crates/continuum-asupersync/tests/support/truncation.rs:92-93, which requires every own-task request to have its own lifecycle `cancel`.

Track absorption provenance. For example, record completion only after `lift_single_cancel` successfully applies `CompleteCancelled`. Require every `alone` task to appear in that completed set. Do not infer the path from the shared terminal state. Add lifecycle-only and all-family splice regressions. The A7 model needs the same correction because its finish also accepts any terminal task.

Failure modes: A corrupt or adversarial wire journal can replace the required single-task end with a region drain. The verifier then certifies a false causal history as conforming.

Edge cases: The defect exists with lifecycle only and with cancellation phases. It applies to created, running, or suspended tasks. A later own-region or ancestor-region drain masks the missing step.

Rollback: Revert the deadline lift slice, or make own-task completion provenance explicit and fail closed until the lifecycle `cancel` occurs.

Monitoring: Count conforming journals where lifecycle `cancel-requested` lacks a matching lifecycle `cancel`. The count must remain zero, even when a later drain lists that task.

Validation: Build a journal with `cancel-requested`, then region cancel, drain, and finalize, without lifecycle `cancel`. Require `Inconclusive(InsufficientTelemetry)` or a typed violation. Repeat with deadline phases present and across every family projection. Require the independent model and lift to agree.

The separate risk:critical human-approval gate remains mandatory. This static review cannot waive it.

data.reason: [HIGH] A later region drain can satisfy the terminal-state check for an own-task cancellation whose required lifecycle cancel step is missing. The lift can return Conforms for a false causal history. See th-1shbkn. The separate risk:critical human-approval gate remains mandatory.

data.body: Fixed in 322a003. Provenance: the lift records ended_alone only when CompleteCancelled succeeds for the task; finish needs every task requested alone in it (live: Inconclusive(InsufficientTelemetry); ended some other way: EndedWithoutOwnCancel). Spec reading, RFC 0026 correction 53 item 6: the own request ends with its own lifecycle cancel within the operation that observed it. So a region event, spawn or other task's step between cancel-requested and cancel is a typed violation (InterruptedOwnCancel), and a complete/fail of that task is EndedWithoutOwnCancel. The RFC item now states this. The A7 model has the same rules from the spec text (ended_alone, OwnCancellationInterrupted, OwnCancellationUnended). Tests: the splice under all 32 projections from created, running and suspended tasks, own and ancestor region; a resume+complete splice; lift and model reject each. Pre-review pass also fixed: family presence is read before the first event (cleanup before phases, deadline request with no deadline, send with no permit), complete after a phase, a poll past the deadline (DeadlineIgnored), Deadline after a request; nine hand-built journals pin these. A7 sweep, truncation sweeps and corpora pass, journal bytes unchanged. just check: all pass except security-review-present.

[HIGH][risk:high] Guard every event family while a deadline cancellation is open

`check_not_interrupted` guards only lifecycle events because only `lifecycle::lift` calls it. Effect, obligation, time, and channel events bypass this guard. After lifecycle `cancel-requested`, the calculus remains `Requested`, so ordinary work is legal until acknowledgement.

A forged wire journal can therefore place `EffectEvent::Committed` between deadline `cancel-requested` and cancellation `requested` or `acknowledged`, then finish the phases and lifecycle `cancel`. The effect lift admits the commit at effect.rs:427-432, and the whole journal returns `Conforms`. Obligation commit or transfer and channel send have the same gap. The binding cannot emit this order: binding.rs:3406-3457 builds request, phases, cleanup, completion, and cancel as one contiguous task batch. The independent A7 model repeats the lifecycle-only guard, so its agreement does not close the gap.

Enforce the deadline request and acknowledgement boundary across every event family. A deadline checkpoint is both request and acknowledgement. Permit only the required phase event before acknowledgement, then cancellation cleanup before completion.

Failure modes: An adversarial or corrupt wire journal gains `Conforms` for impossible post-deadline publication, transfer, or I/O. Downstream consumers can trust a false causal history.

Edge cases: Cover effect reserve, commit, and explicit abort; obligation open, committed discharge, and transfer; channel send or receive; timer scheduling; and same-task or other-task events. Test with and without each projected family.

Rollback: Do not merge this deadline-lift slice until a global event guard exists. The prior target does not claim this single-task deadline binding.

Monitoring: Count non-permitted events observed while an own-task cancellation is open. The count must remain zero for bound journals and conforming lifts.

Validation: Add hand-built adversarial journals for each family across all 32 projections. Each must return a typed violation. Keep legitimate cleanup after acknowledgement and every binding-produced journal conforming. Make the independent model enforce the rule separately.

The separate risk:critical human-approval gate remains mandatory. This static review cannot waive it.

[MEDIUM] Match the projection claim to the exercised corpus

The evidence map says every journal and every projection lifts. The cited test checks all full-family journals, but adds five selected projections only when `journals % 13 == 0` at lines 862-875. The 32-projection test at lines 1282-1305 checks every sleepers log but only every seventh gate log. No test exercises every journal across all 32 projections.

Either run the full cross-product or state the sampled coverage exactly. This evidence is used to support fail-closed projection behavior, so the claim must not exceed the executed cases.

Verified at 322a003. `ended_alone` is recorded only after `CompleteCancelled` succeeds, and region drains plus normal terminal steps call `check_not_absorbed`. The created, running, suspended, own-region, ancestor-region, and normal-end splice regressions cover the original finding across all projections. This closes the shared-terminal-state absorption defect. A separate cross-family interruption finding remains open.

data.body: Verified at 9bbdbf285419. EventBody::lift now calls check_own_cancel_admits before every family dispatch. The guard admits only same-task phases, validated cleanup, and the same task cancel. Cross-family work, clock events, other-task events, and region events now fail as InterruptedOwnCancel. The insertion matrix covers all six families.

Verified at 9bbdbf285419. The evidence now distinguishes 7,572 journals lifted under all 32 event-dropping subsets from 1,092 binding logs replayed under all 32 projections. The test header, test body, and RFC use the same sampled counts.

[HIGH][risk:high] Require phases for every live task reached by a region request

`finish` checks missing phases only for workers whose final model state is `Cancelled`. A worker can receive `RegionCancelRequested`, emit no cancellation event, then take lifecycle `complete` or `fail`. `lifecycle::lift` checks only the reported phase map at crates/continuum-asupersync/src/family/lifecycle.rs:520-528. `RegionTree::advance` deliberately permits ordinary work before acknowledgement at crates/continuum-task/src/region.rs:1095-1215. The later drain excludes this now-terminal worker. A second cancelled worker can supply family presence and valid phases, so every finish check passes and the forged journal returns `Conforms`.

The binding cannot emit that journal. It records each substrate `CancelRequest` at crates/continuum-asupersync/src/binding.rs:2923-2933 when cancellation is observed. A normal end leaves that phase unfinished and the binding refuses it. The tree already retains the missing fact through `cancel_phase` at crates/continuum-task/src/region.rs:915-924.

Require every worker whose calculus cancellation phase is non-active because a region request reached it to have a phase entry when this family is present. Otherwise return typed inconclusive when completeness cannot be proved.

Failure modes: A corrupt wire journal hides a cancellation request, reports normal completion, and receives `Conforms`. Downstream consumers trust a false terminal cause and incomplete telemetry.

Edge cases: Cover `complete` and `fail`, created and running tasks, own-region and ancestor-region requests, and multiple tasks where another task makes the cancellation family present. A task terminal before the region request must remain valid.

Rollback: Revert this cancellation-lift slice, or fail closed for any region-requested worker without a matching phase entry.

Monitoring: Count conforming journals where `tree.cancel_phase(worker)` is non-active but `cancellation.phases` has no worker. The count must remain zero when the family is present.

Validation: Build a two-task journal. After one region request, omit all phases for t0 and complete or fail it. Fully phase and drain t1. Require a typed violation. Keep the family-absent projection and the task-terminal-before-request control conforming.

The separate risk:critical human-approval gate remains mandatory. This static review cannot waive it.

data.body:
[HIGH][risk:high] Reject an own-region cancellation after the task deadline is due

This regional Requested branch checks only the region-implied cause. It never consults the declared deadline or clock. A forged all-family journal can spawn t0 in r1 with deadline 10, begin it, advance to 20, then report RegionCancelRequested(r1), requested(user), acknowledged, cancelled(user), drain, and finalize. The branch accepts user because r1 is the owner. time::check_actor_deadline ignores region and cancellation events, and time::finish has no deadline-cause reconciliation. The journal therefore returns Conforms.

The binding refuses this exact execution as CancelRaced at crates/continuum-asupersync/src/binding.rs:3402-3403. The test at crates/continuum-asupersync/tests/pr14_deadline_cancellation.rs:1283-1306 requires that refusal under every projection. RFC 0026 correction 53 says the due deadline is the stronger cause for an own-region request. Parent cancellation remains the admitted override.

Failure modes: An adversarial wire journal can hide an unsupported deadline/region race behind cause=user. The independent lift then certifies an execution that the binding cannot produce.

Edge cases: Cover created, running, and suspended tasks. Own-region cancellation after the deadline is the defect. Cancellation before the deadline remains valid. Proper-ancestor cancellation remains parent-cancelled and valid. A projection without time cannot decide this fact.

Rollback: Withdraw the deadline binding slice, or make the lift fail closed when an own-region request names a task whose declared deadline is already due.

Monitoring: Count conforming journals with deadline <= now followed by a regional user request for that task. The count must remain zero when time and cancellation are present.

Validation: Hand-build the sequence above and require a typed violation or inconclusive result. Add controls for own-region cancellation before the deadline, proper-ancestor cancellation after it, and projections without time. Compare the lift with the existing binding CancelRaced test.

The separate risk:critical human-approval gate remains mandatory. This static review cannot waive it.

data.reason: HIGH risk:high: the lift accepts an own-region user cancellation after the task deadline is already due, although the binding refuses that execution as CancelRaced. See th-18a2iz.

data.body: Verified at 497fd4a0efc8. lifecycle::lift now calls time::check_cancel_not_raced before mutating the region tree. The check rejects a due own-region task and preserves the ancestor and before-deadline controls.

[HIGH][risk:high] Advance the journal encoding version for new existing-family tags

This range adds lifecycle step tags 6 and 7 at crates/continuum-asupersync/src/family/lifecycle.rs:127-128, cancellation cause tag 3 at crates/continuum-asupersync/src/family/cancellation.rs:111-125, and time event tag 5 at crates/continuum-asupersync/src/family/time.rs:126-143. It leaves ENCODING_VERSION at 1, although lines 37-39 require a bump when an existing family payload changes. An earlier version-1 decoder rejects each new tag as UnknownTag. Therefore, the same version now names two incompatible grammars. The governance claim at tools/governance/reviews/bn-36wy3.toml:40-42 confirms these tags and incorrectly treats unchanged earlier bytes as sufficient.

Failure modes: A new writer emits version-1 deadline evidence that an earlier version-1 verifier rejects. Mixed deployments disagree on whether one content-addressed artifact is valid.

Edge cases: Old journals remain readable by the new decoder. Only journals that use a new tag fail older readers. Cached verifiers and mixed-version fleets expose the split.

Rollback: Withdraw the new wire tags, or advance the encoding version and epoch. Keep an explicit old-version decoder if compatibility is required.

Monitoring: Count decode failures by version and tag. Any UnknownTag from a new writer under version 1 is a compatibility alarm.

Validation: Decode a new deadline journal with the prior target and require an explicit version mismatch, not UnknownTag under version 1. Keep old version-1 golden bytes unchanged and test both decoder generations.

The separate risk:critical human-approval gate remains mandatory. This static review cannot waive it.

[HIGH][risk:high] Require a deadline declaration to be contiguous with its task spawn

The binding always appends TimeEvent::Deadline immediately after the matching TaskSpawned at crates/continuum-asupersync/src/binding.rs:2817-2828. This lift accepts the declaration whenever the task is still Created, regardless of intervening events. A forged journal can spawn t0 without a deadline, advance time from 0 to 5, declare deadline 10 for t0, then begin it. The time lift accepts this sequence. The independent model repeats the same permissive rule at crates/continuum-asupersync/tests/support/primitive_conformance_model.rs:1596-1605 and generates late declarations at lines 2613-2621. No binding execution can emit that order.

Failure modes: An adversarial wire journal can attach a budget retroactively and receive Conforms for evidence outside the binding image.

Edge cases: The task must remain Created, the deadline must be unique and ahead of the current clock. Immediate declarations are valid. Declarations after begin already fail. Journals without the time family make no deadline claim.

Rollback: Withdraw the deadline event, or track spawn adjacency and require Deadline to directly follow the matching TaskSpawned. Apply the same rule independently in the A7 model.

Monitoring: Count conforming Deadline events whose previous event is not the matching TaskSpawned. The count must stay zero.

Validation: Hand-build spawn, unrelated event or clock advance, then Deadline and require a typed violation. Keep immediate declaration and no-deadline spawn controls conforming. Add an independent-model mutant for the adjacency rule.

The separate risk:critical human-approval gate remains mandatory. This static review cannot waive it.

Failure modes: No unresolved path was found that lets projected, truncated, raced, or version-mislabeled evidence return false conformance.
